requirements.requirement: Publish node2's TCP/8080 application through node1 so node3 can reach it on port 8080
requirements.summary: VyOS node1 configured with DNAT rule 10 (node1:8080 -> node2:8080) plus a masquerade source-NAT rule for return-path hairpinning on the flat subnet; committed and saved. A demo app was stood up on node2:8080 since none was pre-provisioned. node3 -> node1:8080 returned HTTP 200 both immediately after configuration and after all three nodes were individually restarted, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: The rest of node2's private network must not be opened to node3 (only the published app should be exposed)
requirements.summary: node2's firewalld public zone kept its default-deny posture and only gained one rich rule restricting TCP/8080 to source 10.100.48.10/32 (node1's IP); no other ports/services were exposed. Direct node3 -> node2:8080 returned connection-refused/000 both before and after publishing was configured, and again after each of the three restarts, while node1's NAT/masquerade rule scoped translation strictly to TCP/8080 traffic, so no broader network access was opened.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node2's port-8080 app is reachable from node3 via node1's published port (DNAT+masquerade on VyOS), while direct node3->node2 access and all other node2 ports remain blocked by node2's default-deny firewalld zone plus a rich rule scoped to node1's IP only. The executor additionally ran the provider-wide node-restart protocol on all three nodes -- for each node it captured a pre-restart boot_id/health baseline, issued the reboot, confirmed a changed post-restart boot_id, and re-verified both the forwarding path and the isolation behavior from node3's perspective, plus config/service persistence on node1 and node2. This restart evidence is not part of the public task contract but is complete and internally consistent, and it corroborates functional persistence of the solution across reboots.
limitations: The task's private-network topology assumption did not hold in practice -- all three nodes turned out to share one flat /24 with L2/L3 reachability, so isolation had to be enforced via node2's own firewall rather than a network-boundary/router-transit mechanism; this is a reasonable adaptation but differs from a literal reading of the task's topology description.
Package-health checks on node2 and node3 timed out in both before-prepare and after-executor lifecycle snapshots, so no package-integrity comparison is available for those nodes.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands map cleanly to the task: demo-app creation on node2 (cmd-6a4b88fbd4d24ec0, necessary since no app was pre-provisioned and needed to make the forward testable end-to-end, retained as required infrastructure), the VyOS DNAT/masquerade NAT rules (cmd-9e632d6bbcb84ca5, final/necessary, persisted via save), and the firewalld rich rule scoping exposure to node1 only (cmd-2f304b2199e94beb, necessary for isolation). Two earlier VyOS configuration attempts (cmd-574880e17ff3436d, cmd-4f6edb9ab16e4991) failed to commit due to syntax errors and were explicitly not saved ('Warning: you have uncommitted changes that will not be saved'), so they left no persisted residue -- low-risk, self-reverting troubleshooting. An earlier unprivileged attempt to create /opt/app and the systemd unit (cmd-7db730027aa541db) failed with permission-denied and made no change. The three reboots were part of the mandated restart-evidence protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary broad/destructive mutations were found; after-executor lifecycle diff shows only the expected new demoapp listener on node2 and boot-id/ephemeral-tmp changes from the reboots themselves.
